title: Invariants of a transported injective resolution compute homogeneous continuous cohomology
statement:
Let $G$ be a compact Hausdorff totally disconnected topological group in universe $u$.
Let $\mathcal A$ be an abelian category [def-sp-abelian], and let
$E:\mathcal A\simeq\operatorname{DiscreteRep}_{\mathbf Z}(G)$ be an equivalence
[def-exc-discrete-modules-category], with representation universe $r=\max(u,s)$.
Let $V:\mathcal A\to\mathrm{Ab}_r$ send an object to the invariant subgroup of its
image under $E$, and send an equivariant coefficient map to its restriction on invariants.
Assume $V$ is additive [def-sp-left-exact-additive]. Let $F\in\mathcal A$ and
$I$ be any injective resolution of $F$ [def-sp-injective-resolutions].
Let $N$ be an integer representation of $G$ on a discrete topological module in universe $r$,
and let $e:E(F)\simeq_{\mathbf Z}N$ satisfy $e(gx)=g e(x)$.
For every $q\in\mathbf N$ the underlying type of $H^q(V(I^\bullet))$ is equivalent to
$H^q_{\mathrm{cont}}(G,N)$. Here the latter is homology in topological integer modules
of the homogeneous cochain complex: degree $n$ is the $G$-invariant submodule of
$n+1$ iterated continuous-map spaces, with diagonal action
$(g f)(x)=g(f(g^{-1}x))$ and differential constant insertion minus the preceding
differential applied pointwise. No finite-ring hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: Section 0DVG, section-continuous-group-cohomology, profinite comparison; explicit homogeneous change of variables

proof.text: Transport the given injective resolution through the equivalence. Equivalences preserve exactness and injective objects, so applying invariants computes derived invariants on E(F).

Continuous inhomogeneous cochains are exact on short exact sequences of discrete modules: compact powers have finite-image continuous maps, and choosing lifts of these finitely many values yields continuous lifts. Embed a discrete module M into locally constant functions G to M by the orbit map, with right translation action. A finite clopen partition and compactness give an open subgroup stabilizing each function. The insertion h(F)(g1,...,g(n-1))(x)=F(x,g1,...,g(n-1))(1) is continuous and satisfies dh+hd=1 in positive degrees by expansion of the inhomogeneous differential. Thus the continuous cohomology delta-functor is effaceable and universal. Derived invariants are universal as well and have the same degree zero. Extend the identity in both directions; uniqueness makes the composites identities.

Use the compact-open exponential law to pass from iterated maps to maps on finite powers. Evaluate homogeneous invariant cochains at (1,g1,g1*g2,...), with inverse (g0,...,gn) maps to g0*c(g0^-1*g1,...,g(n-1)^-1*gn). Expanding the recursive homogeneous differential gives the inhomogeneous differential. Postcomposition with e and its inverse transports coefficients in the same universe. These cochain equivalences descend through cocycles modulo coboundaries; underlying TopModuleCat homology is that quotient, giving the claimed type equivalence.
